questions.prompt: OWASP describes prompt injection. Must the injected text be visible to people?

options.text: Yes, it only works when a person can read the instructions.
options.explanation: OWASP says the opposite. Injected text can be hidden from people and still affect the model.

options.text: No, it only has to be read by the model, so it can be hidden.
options.explanation: Right. OWASP says prompt injections "do not need to be human-visible/readable, as long as the content is parsed by the model."

options.text: Yes, because apps delete all hidden text before the model sees it.
options.explanation: Apps don't promise that. Hidden text on a page or in a file can still reach the model.

questions.prompt: The Claude Help Center lists details to be careful about sharing in a chat. Which is on the list?

options.text: Your favourite food and the city you like best.
options.explanation: These are not on the list. The list is about financial, health, login and confidential data.

options.text: The title of a public news story you want to discuss.
options.explanation: Public facts are not on the list. The list is about private, sensitive details.
Right. The list names financial information, health records, "Passwords or private login credentials" and confidential documents.

questions.prompt: What does the Claude Help Center say about a public link to a chat?

options.text: Anyone who has the link can open it, with no account needed.
options.explanation: Right. The Help Center says anyone with the link can open it, and "No Claude account is required."

options.text: Only people who pay for a plan can open the shared link.
options.explanation: The Help Center says no Claude account is needed at all.

options.text: It also shares every file that you attached to the chat.
options.explanation: The Help Center says attached files are not included in the shared snapshot.
